summary: Wes Goldberg argues that the Warriors' recent draft failures, including lottery picks Jonathan Kuminga, Moses Moody and James Wiseman, have left the team old and struggling at 8-10 after a collapse to the Kings. The core of Curry, Thompson and Green is aging, and the supposed two-timeline plan has not produced young contributors. The piece suggests the team may need to trade Kuminga and Moody and reshape the roster around Curry before the February deadline.
one_line: Golden State's failed draft picks like Kuminga, Moody and Wiseman have left an aging Warriors roster with few young contributors and tough decisions ahead.
key_facts: In June 2021 the Warriors drafted Jonathan Kuminga (G-League Ignite) at No. 7 and Moses Moody (Arkansas) at No. 14, with then-GM Bob Myers presiding.
Kuminga, 21, plays nearly 20 minutes per game but is shooting career lows of 43.8% overall and 19.4% on 3s.
Moody is shooting 38.2% from 3 and is described as a reliable catch-and-shoot threat and earnest defender, but he does little outside his job description.
The Warriors are 8-10 after a collapse to the Kings in Sacramento, where they led by five with 58 seconds left in an In-Season Tournament game; Malik Monk scored five points in the final 37 seconds.
The Warriors' starting five is being outscored by 10.6 points per 100 possessions this season.
Golden State is the league's third-oldest team behind the Bucks and Clippers; Curry is 35, Green 33 and Thompson 33.
In the last nine months the Warriors traded 24-year-old Jordan Poole to the Wizards for 38-year-old Chris Paul, traded Wiseman for 30-year-old Gary Payton II, and signed 29-year-old Dario Saric.
In 2021 they picked Kuminga one pick ahead of Franz Wagner and Moody over Alperen Sengun and Trey Murphy III; in 2020 they took Wiseman No. 2 over LaMelo Ball and Tyrese Haliburton.
Kevon Looney, picked in 2015, is the only indisputable draft success, and Poole is the only other pick to sign a second contract with the team.
Four draftees are on other teams (Patrick Baldwin, Wiseman, Poole, Damian Jones) and four are out of the league (Nico Mannion, Justinian Jessup, Eric Paschall, Jacob Evans).
June's No. 19 pick Brandin Podziemski looks like a base hit so far, but it has only been a month.
Thompson becomes a free agent in seven months, Paul's contract for next season is not guaranteed, and Green's new contract may look worse when he is 37.
Kuminga's $6 million salary plus Payton could build $14.7 million in outgoing salary, while Moody's $3.9 million could sweeten a deal.
New GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. could be tasked with reshaping the roster around Curry before February's trade deadline.
